The device profile has been used across 27 other cards in the past 30 days, with similar cases involving unauthorized online purchases from the same device. The model risk score is unusually low for fraud, but the pattern and customer denial warrant action. Exposure totals $439.61, and connected cards are under monitoring.

sar.narrative: Card C13487-K1 processed three transactions on November 15 and 26, 2016, originating from a Samsung SM-G935F device running Android 7.0 and Chrome 62.0, accessed via an anonymous proxy. The device profile was flagged as new for this account, despite matching a pattern seen across 27 other cards in the past 30 days. The customer confirmed they did not authorize the purchases and still holds the card, reinforcing suspicion. Similar cases (CC-2649, CC-2985, CC-3035) involved unauthorized online purchases from the same device profile, never previously linked to those accounts. The low model risk score (0.05) contrasts with typical fraud thresholds (0.84–0.92), suggesting the model may have missed key behavioral anomalies. The device’s use of an anonymous proxy and its recurrence across multiple accounts aligns with fraudulent activity, likely involving stolen or shared card details. The exposure of $439.61 and the pattern’s consistency with prior cases justify escalation and reporting.
